1. DESIGN. The CTO's ruling @606e7d14ce ADOPTED the object-scoped read the packet declares and BARRED the publisher copy. The packet meets its four conditions: the registry vintage (blob 99b8eeb54f) and the ARN list are printed; the ban comment was amended in the same commit as the statement (@9f21dedfd8); the plans are 0 to destroy and every IAM key is additive; the bucket map is the one registry-derived value the directory root already sets. S94 stays the precondition (_authz/loaders.py:106-114 @4ceb7f8361); pitched to the CTO, carved out of the token.
2. WHY EARLIER PROOFS PASSED. rtf-2 and rtf-8 arm (e) ran the real code IN-PROCESS under operator credentials and the harness environment. The ruling's identity bar binds this order: an arm claiming a served behaviour names its principal, which must be the function's own execution role. The packet's section 9 states it per arm, and the battery prints the identity per arm, marking (a)-(d) and (c-code) as configuration claims.
3. S91 and S96. _authz/served.py:628,649,662 @4ceb7f8361 record internal errors to a None sink. S96 is the same class at the build layer: the served directory-search zip carried a hand-placed CRLF member that no committed tree state reproduces, visible only to a rebuild from HEAD, which failed closed. Remedied under the issuer's ruling (i): one staged_from object @2b1c672e1f, and the rebuild's 10 of 10 members equal their committed blobs.
